summary: Rerun the 12 blocked Free checks on first-time accounts, and check five committed fixes in a real browser

free.basic: W-1 Sign up, age step, sign in, sign out and back in
free.observed_result:
The public sign-up form itself was NOT tested (its human check cannot be completed in this browser); that step is blocked. Everything after account creation worked. Signed in at /login with the email and code 424242, then went through the age step, the terms step and reached a working chat on the Free plan.

- Age step: an empty submit shows "Enter your age in years to continue." Opening /chat while the age step was unfinished sent me back to the age step, so the protected workspace stayed unavailable. I did not try an under-18 age, in case it locks the account. Entering 34 was accepted.
- Terms step ("Finish signing in"): Continue stays disabled until the terms box is ticked.
- First chat: a 600-word story streamed and finished, and the chat was titled and listed in Recents. Stop pressed halfway through a second answer kept the partial text with "Response stopped." and "Try again", and it survived a reload. A plain follow-up asking for a 1500-word history first showed a clarifying-question card (see problem 5).
- Offline: an "Offline" pill and a banner ("Your draft is saved here and can be sent after you reconnect") appeared, and the draft sent correctly once back online ("OK").
- Sign out and back in: Log out went to the marketing home page, and /chat while signed out went to /login. Signing in again with the same email went straight to /chat with no age step, showing the same identity, the Free plan and the same chat. Reload kept everything.
- Why partial: problems 1 to 6 below, mainly the false "Agent run failed" notification after Stop and the leftover "Writing response" row.
- Handoff times: each handoff had settled by my first screenshot, within the 3 to 6 second fixed waits I used. These are not precise.
free.first_words_ms: Time to first words, two readings. The server log shows llm_ttft_observed for (model name) at 840 ms and 1765 ms, but I cannot tell which line was mine because other testers were running. My own stopwatch: the answer was already streaming at my first poll, 3 seconds or less after Enter.
free.stream_and_finish: The 600-word story streamed and finished completely. Stop mid-stream worked and kept the partial text. A visible "Writing response" row with an empty checkbox stayed above the partial answer after Stop, and a clarifying-question card for a plain follow-up showed above it (see problems).
free.recovery_and_sync: Reload mid-conversation and after Stop kept the chat and the partial answer. Offline kept the draft, and sending after reconnect worked. Sign out and back in returned the same account and chat. The theme choice (Light) also persisted across sign-out. The age and terms steps did not reappear on the second sign-in. Only at the age step was protected-workspace blocking checked, by opening /chat; cancel via "Sign out" there was not exercised.
free.light_dark_and_size: Light (default) and Dark checked at 1280 and 390 on the chat screen; nothing overlapped, was cut off or was unreadable. At 390 the composer shows only icons (the model name is hidden) and Share and Upgrade are not in the header, which looked intentional. The login page was checked in light at 1280 only. After Escape from Settings, a thin blue line showed above the account row in dark at 1280 (probably a focus ring).
free.leader_comparison: Compared from my knowledge of ChatGPT and Claude. First-run is cleaner than the leaders' because the age and terms steps are short, the Free upgrade is a plain label, and the offline draft banner is as good as theirs. Where AGI is visibly worse: pressing Stop raises an "Agent run failed" notification, which neither ChatGPT nor Claude does, and a plain "write a 1500 word history" follow-up got a clarifying question where both leaders would just write it. The greeting uses the raw email-local-part as a name.

free.basic: W-12 Memory: tell it something, see it used in a new chat, delete it

Asking the chat to remember "My sample label is hazel kite" while it is off gives a clear message ("memory is off. You can manage saved memories in Settings under Memory"), not an error. After turning Persistent memory on and repeating the request, Settings shows 1 saved memory, "My sample label is hazel kite", "Added by you · Updated Nov 24". Uploading route-brief.pdf as a project knowledge file failed twice with "Something went wrong on our side. Try again shortly." The server log shows a 500 with column "storage_targets" of relation "project_knowledge_files" does not exist. The column is added by repo migration 0419, so the local test DB looks behind the build. That makes the scripted file step blocked by this machine's setup, and I could not verify it. Workaround, not the scripted path: attaching the PDF inside a project chat gave "The route brief names Cedar Bay, code VELA-74. END-42". The first in-project question, asked with no file in the project, got a clarifying card ("Which route brief should I check?") with no END-42 on it. A plain follow-up ("Just name one primary colour.") gave "Blue. END-42". The unrelated chat answered "Madrid is the capital of Spain. I don't have access to details from your other projects in this chat..." with no END-42 and no project content.

The project instruction persisted after Save and reopening settings.
